open_obligations: Check for which widths q the 2^(3q) factor keeps the estimator circuits polynomial in size.
Check whether the soundness theorem rules out obfuscation as Buhl et al. define it.
Note the guarantee bounds an expectation over inputs drawn from mu (average-case); check whether Brown-Cohen et al. list this as a limitation.

Note that the soundness theorem only shows that, for each prover strategy, an estimator circuit of the stated size exists that may query a function in the class A; it gives no polynomial-time algorithm for constructing the prover or the estimator.
out.other_title: Open: does prover-estimator debate avoid obfuscation, and are its debaters poly-time?
out.rationale: Buhl et al. list as open whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscation and whether its debaters can be built in polynomial time. Theorem 6.1 (soundness) gives, for every prover, an estimator among circuits of size O(q 2^(3q) n d^2 / eta^2) with oracle access to the prover that caps a dishonest prover's payoff, and stresses that stability is needed only for completeness; the size bound is exponential in width q.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscated arguments and how large the honest estimator must be

text: Theorem 6.1 (soundness) states that, with B the set of circuits of size O(q 2^(3q) n d^2 / eta^2) that may query a function A in the class at each gate, for every strategy A there exists B in that set such that the expected value of V^{A,B}(x) over inputs is at most P[A(x) = L(x)]/rho^(d+1) + eta. The authors note that L is required to admit an A-provable, rho-stable decomposition only in the completeness case, which means a dishonest debater A may produce an incorrect decomposition into queries for some input.
title: Theorem 6.1 soundness: efficient estimator caps a dishonest prover's payoff
